edits.content:
# Challenge-sensitive progression and combat

## Research and design boundary

Official Godot documentation describes _Input before GUI routing and _UnhandledInput after GUI consumption: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/inputs/inputevent.html . The target repair intercepts only the configured target key during active world input; chat and menus retain navigation.

Blizzard's published Diablo II experience rules reduce rewards for large level gaps and reduce advancement at higher levels: https://classic.battle.net/diablo2exp/basics/experience.shtml . These principles inform the separation of practice and advancement. The equations below are original KAIRNFALL tuning, not copied Blizzard constants or claims of optimal balance. Actual playtime, all class matchups and long-term economy still need playtesting.

## Experience equations

Let P be current overall player level, M be target monster level, and S be the trained skill level.

```text
b = floor((P - 1) / 10)
pacing(P) = 0.25 / (1 + 0.14*b + 0.035*b*b)
g = max(0, P - M - 3)
practice(P,M) = max(0.04, 1 / (1 + (g/8)^3))
encounterCredit(P,M) = max(0.005, exp(-0.24*g))
mastery(S,M) = clamp((30 - (S-M))/30, 0.05, 1)
combatSkillXP = baseXP * practice(P,M) * mastery(S,M) * classAffinity
overallContribution = awardedSkillXP * pacing(P) * encounterCredit(P,M)
```

Class affinity remains 1.10 for an affiliated skill and 1 otherwise. Fractions accumulate before integer awards. Tiny hits do not each receive a free one-point award. When a monster is 20 levels lower, practice is approximately 9.4% of base before mastery/affinity; its additional overall encounter factor is approximately 1.69%. Targets within three levels have no gap penalty. Fighting a much stronger target does not create an uncapped experience multiplier.

Pacing changes at levels 11, 21, 31, and so on. The same pacing applies to the overall contribution of noncombat training, while noncombat raw skill awards retain their previous calculation. This prevents crafting or movement XP from silently bypassing the requested overall slowdown. No monster health, damage, armor, aggro, or loot definition is inflated when the player reaches a band.

Saved raw skill XP stays intact. A new server-owned PracticeOnlyXp field records the part of future skill XP that does not count toward overall growth. Missing fields in legacy characters default to zero, preserving their earned levels. Fractional practice and overall credits serialize with the character. All 60 skills at their cap retain the existing terminal overall-level milestone. The previous overall XP-to-level mapping remains in use on credited XP; it is not reapplied destructively to past progress.

Direct hits, delayed hits and kill/defensive training share the authoritative helper. Support actions retain their existing zone-difficulty input; they are not advertised as individual-target reward estimates. Trade, inventory and replay validation remain in the server path.

## Combat equations

```text
physicalMastery(S) = 1 + 0.9*S/(S+75)
spellMastery(S) = 1 + 0.75*S/(S+100)
physicalBase = weaponPower + 0.65*strength + physicalBonus
spellBase = 7 + 1.1*intellect + 0.4*weaponPower + spellBonus
mitigatedDamage = rawDamage * 100/(100 + max(armor,0))
                  * (1 - clamp(resistance,-0.5,1))
```

The new mastery factors have diminishing gains and fixed bounds. Existing critical chance/damage caps, element modifiers, weather, vulnerability, shield handling and actual-health damage caps remain. No extra random miss system or opaque level-based damage multiplier was added. Armor 100 still halves unresisted incoming raw damage. More armor reduces damage but cannot make it negative.

## Interface

The vitals panel shows the current overall-credit rate and next ten-level boundary. The selected-target panel shows challenge category, practice rate and overall credit. Its tooltip explains the order of those factors. Raw skill XP feedback remains separate. Native checks verify those labels at 1280x720 and 1920x1080, including non-overlap with the objective tracker.

## Verification

ChallengeProgressionChecks covers band boundaries, 20-level weaker enemies, accumulated fractions, legacy levels, serialization, exact replay, real kill rewards, finite/monotone formulas, and 50 progression scenarios. Outputs go to artifacts/experience/balance/xp-curves.json. Existing security, saved-object, database, native control and live-client suites remain required. The final dated session handoff records actual results. These equations are implemented design decisions; a passing unit or native test is not a human balance acceptance.
